ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The diagram below shows the circular face of a clock with radius $20$ cm and a circular disk with radius $10$ cm externally tangent to the clock face at $12$ o'clock. The disk has an arrow painted on it, initially pointing in the upward vertical direction. Let the disk roll clockwise around the clock face. At what point on the clock face will the disk be tangent when the arrow is next pointing in the upward vertical direction?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a large circular clock face with hour marks and numbers, with 12 at the top. A smaller circular disk is externally tangent to the clock face at the 12 o'clock point. Inside the smaller disk, an arrow is painted pointing straight upward. A curved arrow to the right indicates that the smaller disk rolls clockwise around the outside of the clock face. Reasoning: The clock radius is 20 cm and the disk radius is 10 cm. Since the disk remains externally tangent to the clock face, the disk center moves on a circle centered at the clock center with radius 20 + 10 = 30 cm. Let the tangency point move clockwise through central angle theta from 12 o'clock. Then the disk center travels arc length 30theta. Rolling without slipping means the disk rotates through angle equal to distance traveled divided by its radius: 30theta / 10 = 3theta. The arrow next points upward when the disk has made one full rotation, so 3theta = 2pi. Thus theta = 2pi/3 = 120 degrees. Each hour mark is 30 degrees, so 120 degrees clockwise from 12 is 4 hour marks. Therefore the disk is tangent at 4 o'clock.

Let the tangency point move clockwise through central angle theta from 12. The disk center travels arc length 30 theta, and for rolling without slipping the disk's absolute rotation angle is this length divided by its radius, so rotation = 30 theta / 10 = 3 theta. The arrow next points upward after one full rotation, so 3 theta = 2 pi, giving theta = 2 pi / 3 = 120 degrees. On the clock face, 120 degrees clockwise from 12 is 4 hour marks, so the tangency point is 4 o'clock.

From the text, the fixed clock radius is 20 cm and the rolling disk radius is 10 cm, so the disk center is 30 cm from the clock center. Moving from one hour mark to the next is a 30 degree central angle, or pi/6 radians, so the disk center moves arc length 30(pi/6) = 5pi cm.
